Description - UploadToken

Issues an upload ticket for one file: key, stamp, the upload server (host:port, varies per call) and locale. The client then posts the file to http://<server>/file/ (see uploadFile) or, for an interrupted upload, first asks GET /resume/check/.

Live: the folder id is not validated when the ticket is issued.

When the client sends it: uploader start, and again after a failed resume. Session-bound.

Routing. The path item declares the server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, so this operation resolves to http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/UploadToken. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the SOAPAction header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (.svc/UploadToken) does not work (a:DestinationUnreachable, see soapRestStylePath).

Wire format. POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/UploadToken (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (Content-Encoding: gzip).

Path notes

SOAP operation UploadToken. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on SOAPAction and ignores the ?op=/UploadToken query.

Parameters

Parameters of UploadToken
NameInRequiredTypeDescriptionExample
SOAPActionheaderrequiredstring = "http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/UploadToken"

WCF dispatch key. The client sends it unquoted (SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/UploadToken); a quoted value works too. Missing or unknown actions give a:ActionNotSupported.

http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/UploadToken
Content-Encodingheaderoptionalstring one of "gzip"

Present when the body is gzip-compressed ([network] soap-use-gzip=true in the default config; zlib level -1, windowBits 31). Accepted by the service (Auth/success vs Auth/success-uncompressed-request).

Schema

Schema UploadTokenRequestEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required UploadTokenRequestEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 request envelope for UploadToken: <s:Envelope><s:Body><UploadToken xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/">…. No SOAP header is ever sent; xmlns:i is declared on the operation element only when a nil value is present.

    • @s:encodingStyle string optional = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" namespace http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

      SOAP 1.1 encodingStyle attribute. The real client always writes it; the service accepts the envelope with or without it.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one operation element; no other content (this also makes the per-operation envelopes mutually exclusive).

      • <UploadToken> object required UploadTokenRequest xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

        Operation element UploadToken in http://chomikuj.pl/ (trailing slash is mandatory: with http://chomikuj.pl the parameters are not matched, see Service/wrong-operation-namespace).

        • <token> string required Token

          Session token. Always the first child.

        • <folderId> integer (int32) required

          Target folder. Not validated when the ticket is issued (UploadToken/nonexistent-folder).

        • <fileName> string required

          Name of the file to upload.

Responses - 200, 500

200

SOAP response envelope. HTTP 200 is used for every service-level outcome, including errors: check UploadTokenResult/status. Compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip) when the request accepts gzip.

Schema text/xml

Schema UploadTokenResponseEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required UploadTokenResponseEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 response envelope for UploadToken: <s:Envelope><s:Body><UploadTokenResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><UploadTokenResult …>.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one response element; no other content.

      • <UploadTokenResponse> object required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/
        • <UploadTokenResult> object required UploadTokenResult

          Result element; declares xmlns:i (XML Schema instance, for i:nil) and xmlns:a.

          • <a:status> string required Status xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Outcome of the call. The client accepts only Ok; BadToken triggers a re-login, anything else is an error.

            7 values
            • "Ok" Success. The only value the client treats as success.
            • "BadToken" Unknown, logged-out or otherwise invalid token. The client re-authenticates (Auth) once per message (message-relog-count=1) and resends the message with the new token; session-bound messages are dropped.
            • "Forbidden" Auth: user name does not exist. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "PermissionError" Auth: wrong password for an existing user. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "Error" Generic failure. Usually carries a reason in errorMessage (e.g. EmptyName, NameExistsAtDestination); FolderFiles with an unknown disposition returns Error with errorMessage nil (FolderFiles/invalid-disposition).
            • "NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder" RemoveFolder with force=false on a folder that contains files, or on an unknown/removed folder id.
            • "WrongDisposition" FolderFiles: the disposition is a known value but not allowed for this call (download).
          • <a:errorMessage> string required nullable (i:nil) ErrorMessage xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Error detail for status=Error; nil otherwise.

          • <a:key> string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Upload key (32 characters); sent as the key part and as ?key= of the resume check. Secret.

          • <a:stamp> string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Numeric ticket stamp (18-digit, tick-based); sent as the time part and used as the multipart boundary suffix !CHB<stamp>. Secret.

          • <a:server> string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Upload server host:port, varies per call (e.g. s6122.chomikuj.pl:8084).

          • <a:locale> string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Locale for the upload server; sent as the locale part. Returned even for BadToken.

500 SoapFault

WCF SOAP fault (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, not compressed). Possible for every SOAP operation: an empty or malformed body gives a:InternalServiceFault, an undeserialisable value a:DeserializationFailed, an unknown or missing SOAPAction a:ActionNotSupported. Operations with an operation-specific captured fault document it inline instead.

Schema text/xml

Schema SoapFaultEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SoapFaultEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 fault envelope (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, never gzip-compressed).

    • <s:Body> object required
      • <s:Fault> object required SoapFault

        The fault.

        • <faultcode> string required no namespace

          Qualified fault code with its own namespace declaration on the element: a:InternalServiceFault and a:DeserializationFailed (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/net/2005/12/windowscommunicationfoundation/dispatcher), a:ActionNotSupported and a:DestinationUnreachable (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2005/05/addressing/none).

        • <faultstring> object required no namespace

          Human-readable message. DeserializationFailed names the parameter and CLR type, which is how the contract was established.

          • @xml:lang string required namespace http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace

            Language of the message (en-US).

          • text content string required

            Message text.

Security notes - findings that concern UploadToken

  • S-05 Low-Medium Silent fallbacks instead of errors: Folders with an unknown folderId returns the root; MoveFolder to an unknown parent moves the folder to the root (Ok); UploadToken with an unknown folderId returns Ok.

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
